# The seven labs and what each one is for

## The seven labs

Each lab has a kit. Every build runs on your own material or a practice file, and both take the same steps. Before the session, save the kit and its practice files into your Kits folder, whether you'll use your own material or the practice file, so you can ask Claude about them. The one exception is the Lab 4 practice key, which stays outside your AI-Labs folder.

### Lab 1: First safe win

One small piece of real writing, checked and ready to send, plus your AI-Labs folder and an AGENTS.md file that Claude writes by interviewing you.

Monday, September 28 · Friday, October 2

**Before the session:** if you did Start here (see hub-start.md), your Lab 1 files are already in your AI-Labs folder and there's nothing more to set up. This card is what happens in the room. If you saved the Lab 1 kit file on or before September 28, save it once more on Cowork, because it was updated, and drag it into Kits, choosing Replace. If it saves with "(1)" in the name, rename it first.

**How your room works:** about eight people from four organizations, with a facilitator. Each of you works on your own computer with your own Claude, your colleague included: your own interview, your own AGENTS.md, your own piece of writing, checked by a fresh Claude session and then by you. Bring one small piece of real writing each, or use the practice thread. Afterward, email your AGENTS.md to your colleague and read theirs.

**Lab 1 kit**: What happens in the session, step by step, and the homework for the week after. If you did Start here, there's nothing more to set up: the kit starts with today's steps, and setup sits in its own section at the end for anyone who skipped it. (lab-1.md)

**Need a file again? The Lab 1 kit, the practice email thread, the interview prompt, and the ship log for the browser version**

Save the Lab 1 kit as a file: KIT-Lab1-First-Safe-Win.md (lab-1.md)

**Practice file: program update email thread**: Only for anyone who doesn't bring their own writing. Made-up emails from a fictional nonprofit; in the lab, Claude turns them into a short board update and you check it against the emails.

**Starter AGENTS.md**: The interview prompt Claude uses to write your AGENTS.md in the session, and the six empty headings.

**Starter ship log**: For the browser route only: save it into Outputs as ship-log.md before the lab. In Cowork, prompt 1 makes it for you.

### Lab 2: Writing and the org brain

One real piece of writing in your organization's voice, or a compliance matrix for a funder's request for proposals (RFP), with your org brain saved along the way: plain text files that tell Claude how your organization sounds.

Monday, October 5 · Friday, October 9

**Today: Claude desktop → Cowork.** [Install the guide](https://github.com/chrisjarviscan/wf-lab-guide/blob/main/START-HERE.md), choose your `AI-Labs` folder, then say:

`I’m ready to begin Lab 2.`

Claude welcomes you, checks the files actually connected to this session, and handles the folder and file work. It asks one short question at a time and leads you from voice notes to a draft, then checks, saves and reopens your work. It pauses for your approval of the voice and facts. If access is missing, it tells you what is needed; help happens individually.

Use permitted public material or practice; remove personal details before sharing. You choose the voice and verify the facts. Minimum today: saved voice notes and approved voice rules. Practice stays separate and labeled practice; your own voice is unfinished until you use your real material.

Using your browser? Say the same start sentence. Claude uses visible Project files or interviews you, then creates files for download where tools allow. It cannot edit your computer’s folder or update Project files automatically.

The Lab 2 worksheet (lab-2.md) is a reference if you want it. You do not need to read it first or choose the next prompt.

**Lab 2 kit**: Start with “I’m ready to begin Lab 2.” Claude checks connected files and leads the work one question at a time, handling files and pausing for your approvals. This worksheet is an optional reference. (lab-2.md)

**Practice file: org brain starter pack**: Documents from BrightPath, a fictional nonprofit: its mission, two writing samples, outcomes and a practice RFP. It takes the same steps as your own documents.

### Lab 3: Board-ready reporting and the second chair

One report section taken through draft, critique and revision, and a saved second chair that reads drafts the way your most skeptical board member would.

Monday, October 12 · Friday, October 16

**Lab 3 kit**: Draft, critique and revise one report section, from your own reporting input or the practice mess pack. (lab-3.md)

**Practice file: the mess pack**: A fictional nonprofit's meeting notes, partial sheet and emails for a board update. Save it into Kits, whichever material you choose.

### Lab 4: Data, clean and extract

A spreadsheet cleaned by Claude, your own recurring one or the practice sheet, with every change in a change log you've checked, the organization names back in, and a cleanup recipe for next month. People's names never go into Claude, and organization names reach it only as placeholders like ORG-01.

Monday, October 19 · Friday, October 23

**Lab 4 kit**: Step by step: a copy of your sheet with its headers checked, your placeholder key, a clean on 10 rows first, your own count and your cleanup recipe. (lab-4.md)

**Practice file: messy grants sheet**: A fictional funder's grants export with the kind of mess a real export has. Save it in AI-Labs/Kits; the steps are the same as for your own sheet.

**Practice placeholder key (save it outside AI-Labs, never in Kits)**: Matches each placeholder, like ORG-01, to a fictional organization's name in the practice sheet. Keys never go near Claude, so save this one in a folder outside your AI-Labs folder, even though it's practice.

### Lab 5: Numbers to narrative to deck

Checked insights, a checked narrative and a slide outline for an upcoming meeting, yours or the practice set's, plus a slide deck (.pptx) started with Claude and finished at home if needed.

Monday, October 26 · Friday, October 30

**Lab 5 kit**: Numbers to insights to a checked narrative to a slide outline to a deck, each checked before the next, with your own numbers or the practice set. (lab-5.md)

**Practice file: grants sheet, cleaned**: A fictional funder's 57 cleaned grants from 2024 and 2025, the numbers for the practice set.

**Practice file: context for the committee**: What the practice numbers can't show, and the funder's quarterly committee the deck is for.

### Lab 6: Skills, research and the wider toolbox

Your second chair saved as a skill and run on a real draft, and a one-page summary of a Claude Research report, with its claims checked at the source.

Monday, November 2 · Friday, November 6

**Lab 6 kit**: Saving your second chair as a skill, running Research and checking it at the source, step by step. The map of other AI tools is at the end. (lab-6.md)

**Practice file: grants sheet, cleaned (from Lab 5)**: The numbers behind the practice narrative you wrote in Lab 5, for running your skill on it. Save it into Kits if it isn't there already, whichever draft you pick.

**Practice file: context for the committee (from Lab 5)**: The context file that goes with those numbers. Save it into Kits if it isn't there already, whichever draft you pick.

### Lab 7: Build session and 90-day roadmap

A written workflow a colleague could run without you, timed before and after and shown to your room, and a plan for the next 90 days.

Monday, November 9 · Friday, November 13

**Lab 7 kit**: Writing your workflow down, checking it, and your 90-day plan. The workflow can be your own or the one you ran on the Lab 4 and 5 practice files; both take the same steps. (lab-7.md)
